away.headline: Colts’ Sauce Gardner news could affect his NFL trade deadline value
away.blurb: According to reports, Gardner has been diagnosed with a mild calf strain and is considered week-to-week after undergoing an MRI. The injury occurred during the third quarter of Indianapolis’ 26-20 loss to the Tennessee Titans on Sunday, creating uncertainty about when the star defensive back will return. If Indianapolis decides to sell players before the deadline, Gardner could attract interest because of his age, experience and defensive credentials. Nevertheless, his injury could complicate negotiations and potentially limit the offers available to the Colts. The NFL trade deadline could become more complicated for the Indianapolis Colts after cornerback Sauce Gardner suffered a calf injury that may affect his availability and potential trade value. With the Colts sitting at 2-4, the team could consider moving valuable players before the trade deadline. However, Gardner’s latest injury could make finding a suitable trade partner more difficult. MORE: NFL contenders & pretenders after Week 6 Gardner’s injury creates trade deadline questions Gardner, 25, was named NFL Defensive Rookie of the Year in 2022 after an outstanding start to his professional career. His reputation as a premier cornerback made him a significant acquisition for Indianapolis last season. Last year, the Colts sent two first-round picks and wide receiver Adonai Mitchell to the New York Jets in exchange for Gardner, demonstrating how highly the organization valued his abilities. However, the investment has yet to deliver the results Indianapolis hoped for. Through six games this season, Gardner has recorded 17 total tackles, including 13 solo tackles, as the Colts have struggled to find consistency. The latest injury is particularly concerning because Gardner also dealt with problems involving the same calf last season, suffering injuries in Weeks 13 and 17. Although the current strain is considered mild, the week-to-week designation leaves questions about his recovery timeline. Any potential suitor would likely want clarity regarding his health before committing significant trade assets to acquire him. MORE: 3 NFL teams that should be worried after Week 6 Colts face tough test without their star cornerback Indianapolis will have to move forward without Gardner when it faces the undefeated Minnesota Vikings in Week 7 on Sunday. Minnesota enters the matchup with a 5-0 record, presenting a difficult challenge for a Colts defense already dealing with uncertainty surrounding one of its most important players. The coming weeks could determine whether Indianapolis attempts to strengthen its roster or shifts its focus toward future seasons. For Gardner, a successful recovery will be crucial regardless of whether he remains with the Colts beyond the trade deadline. His health could ultimately play a significant role in shaping both his immediate future and Indianapolis’ plans moving forward.

away.headline: Colts key playmaker remains sidelined with injury
away.blurb: The Indianapolis Colts are coming off their second-straight and fourth total loss of the 2026 season, and it’s safe to say a large reason why is because they were without one of their top playmakers. Unfortunately, his return to the field remains unknown. The Colts selected Warren with the No. 14 overall pick in the 2025 NFL Draft out of Penn State, where he won the John Mackey Award as the nation’s top tight end in 2024. Related Articles Bears React to NFL Announcement for QB Caleb Williams Following His Return According to Myles Simmons of Pro Football Talk, Colts second-year tight end Tyler Warren was still sidelined on Wednesday with a groin injury. It’s certainly not the news Colts fans were hoping to hear as the team is schedule to take on the undefeated Minnesota Vikings in Week 7. However, head coach Shane Steichen did provide a bit of a promising update after practice. “He’s progressing really well, but I’ll defer to the injury report this week on a lot of those guys,” Steichen said . It can’t be understated how much Warren means to the Colts’ offense. Despite missing Week 6, he still leads the team with 30 catches to go along with 213 yards and two touchdowns. In the meantime, the Colts will have to continue relying on veteran wide receivers Josh Downs, Keenan Allen and Laquon Treadwell as well as backup tight end Mo Alie-Cox. It didn’t take Warren long to establish himself as one of the best up-and-coming tight ends in the league, either. As a rookie, Warren racked up 76 catches for 817 yards and four touchdowns. home.blurb: LP = Limited participant in practice. DNP = Did not participate in practice. Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. Historically, 95% of players designated probable are active and played on game day. Questionable = the league defines a Questionable injury designation as being 'uncertain' of whether the player will play or not. This replaces the former definition of having a 50% chance of playing. Historically, 70-75% of players with a Questionable injury designation were active and played on game day. Doubtful = The league defines a Doubtful injury designation to mean the player is unlikely to participate in the game. In practical terms, teams use the designation when a player has less than a 50% chance to suit up, and active game appearances from this designation remain rare. Historically only around 6% of players with a Doubtful designation are active and played on game day. Out = will not play. Players with this designation are not active on game day and league rules prohibit them from playing. For the Colts, they have seven starters who did not practice Wednesday due to injury. They include linebacker Bryce Boettcher, cornerback Sauce Gardner, right guard Matt Gonglaves, punter Rigoberto Sanchez, right tackle Jalen Travis, slot cornerback Justin Walley, and tight end Tyler Warren. Slot Cornerback Justin Walley's injury is new. Not much else is known at this point, but his not practicing and Sauce Gardner already likely out on Sunday could leave the Colts' struggling secondary pretty thin at cornerback. We'll see how it plays out with injury updates tomorrow and Friday. Both teams are looking to keep their seasons from going completely off the rails, so let’s make some predictions for this Week 7 matchup. THREE BOLD PREDICTIONS Malik Washington Sets a Season High in Receiving Yards Sunday will mark the return of rookie receiver Caleb Douglas, who has missed the past three games with an ankle injury. Adding his size to the top of the depth chart should bump everyone else to a more natural position, and there may be no bigger benefactor than Malik Washington. Washington has quietly put together an impressive third season, tallying 50 or more scrimmage yards in four of his first five games. He has also established himself as a favorite target of quarterback Malik Willis, who has thrown his way 36 times this year (more than double the second-place mark). As Miami looks for sustainability, targeting Washington underneath seems like a potential solution, and he has the agility to make defenders miss in space. His ascension, Douglas’ return, and Willis likely needing quick answers against a Jets defense that ranks eighth in blitz percentage is a recipe for a big day for Miami’s most experienced receiver. Both Quarterbacks are Sacked 3+ Times This matchup features two passers who have done a poor job mitigating pressure this season. Both rank top 12 in time to throw, top three in pressure rate allowed, and top five in sack percentage. The Jets are well equipped to take advantage of Malik Willis’ indecision. Their defense ranks in the top eight in pressure rate, and is tied for sixth in total sacks through six weeks. The Dolphins, on the other hand, have been inept up front. Their four sacks are half the next-lowest team in the NFL, and all four came against Kyler Murray and the Minnesota Vikings in Week 4. With two weeks to prepare, a quarterback who is willing to hang in the pocket, and the potentially dumb luck that Miami’s sacks have come in a bunch, this feels like a perfect opportunity for the Dolphins’ defensive front to make its mark, even if Malik Willis’ play leads to a similar outcome on the opposite side of the ball. Ollie Gordon Makes a Game-Changing Explosive Run Ollie Gordon's development in year two has been a revelation. His footwork looks substantially better than it did in 2025, and he’s made the most of his elevated opportunity. Gordon’s rushing yards over expected per attempt is ninth among qualified rushers, per NextGenStats. The Jets have a very sound defense on a per-run basis. Their EPA per rush allowed is tied for third best in football, and they’re right around the middle of the pack in terms of yards-per-attempt. They have, however, struggled to stop runs in the backfield. Their stuffed run rate is seventh-lowest, and they’re allowing over a yard and a half before contact per carry, which ranks ninth-worst. Miami’s massive offensive line has opened up big lanes for Gordon in recent weeks. He has a 20+ yard carry in each of the last two games. Now, against a defense that particularly struggles to generate displacement, it wouldn’t be shocking to see the left-side duo of Paul and Proctor give Gordon a runway that he can use to get downhill and put his massive frame to work against New York’s defensive backs. picks.headline: Four Bold Predictions for Dolphins-Jets

Stowers Sat, October 17, 2026 at 5:47 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Miami's Oct. 25 visit to MetLife Stadium matches two limited offenses and two teams trying to define their seasons. The Jets are early 4.5-point favorites, but the Dolphins' improving rushing attack creates room for several bold predictions. Ollie Gordon II will rush for at least 100 yards. Gordon has totaled 188 yards in two starts since De'Von Achane went on injured reserve. Miami's 217-yard performance against Cincinnati should convince the coaching staff to keep the offense on the ground. New York has been much stronger against the pass than the run, which gives Gordon a favorable path to volume. Malik Willis will produce two touchdowns and no more than one turnover. This is the prediction that would change the game. Willis threw two interceptions and lost a fumble against Cincinnati, but the bye gives Miami time to reduce his difficult reads. Designed runs and play-action can turn his mobility into production while limiting risky throws. Miami will record at least three sacks. The Dolphins have only four sacks through five games, making this the boldest defensive call. Hafley's staff has two weeks to design pressure packages against Geno Smith. A healthier edge rotation and more aggressive use of linebackers could finally create the disruption missing against Cincinnati. The game will be decided by three points or fewer. The early total sits below 40 at several books. New York averages 18.6 points and Miami 14. The Jets have the stronger defense, while the Dolphins have the more productive recent running game. Neither team has shown enough passing explosiveness to create confidence in a runaway. A reasonable projection is Jets 20, Dolphins 17, but that margin leaves the upset door open. If Miami wins the turnover battle, Gordon controls the tempo and special teams avoid another disastrous start, the Dolphins can reverse the score. Bold predictions are not promises. They are matchup-based possibilities. The first three require Miami to emerge from the bye with a more disciplined offense and a more creative defense. If those changes appear, the fourth prediction should follow naturally.

away.headline: Caleb Douglas could return to Miami Dolphins lineup against New York Jets
away.blurb: “Caleb will be limited [in practice] today. You know, we’ll see how he looks today and progress to Wednesday, but I think there’s optimism there. Let’s see how it goes today, and if he can get ramped up on Wednesday, it would be good to get him back out there.” The Miami Dolphins had a much needed bye week this past weekend. Multiple players have been banged up, including standout rookie receiver Caleb Douglas. It seems the added rest has been a good thing for the young pass catcher, as according to head coach Jeff Hafley, Douglas has a chance to suit up against the New York Jets on the road this upcoming Sunday. During his press availability on Monday morning, head coach Jeff Hafley was asked about Douglas’ potential to practice this week. Hafley, with a smile on his face, would go on to speak about what Miami missed on offense without Douglas in the mix. “Just kind of looking back through the last couple of weeks, some of the things that he did, we’ve missed him. And to see a rookie kind of have to start and stop like that, not ideal. But, he’s worked really hard and it would be very great to get him back.” We will keep a close eye on Douglas’ practice participation as the week unfolds, but as of Monday afternoon, his availability seems to be pointing in a positive direction in regards to playing this Sunday.

away.headline: Dolphins-Jets Injury Update: Bye Leaves Key Miami Questions Open
away.blurb: Miami's Week 6 bye prevents the Dolphins from issuing a conventional Friday game-status report, so no player should be labeled officially out or questionable for the Oct. 25 Jets game unless the club has made that designation. The week still produced several important health developments. Right guard Jonah Savaiinaea did not participate in Tuesday's voluntary practice after leaving the Cincinnati game with an ankle injury. Linebacker Jordyn Brooks, edge rusher Robert Beal Jr., cornerback Reese Taylor, running back Jaylen Wright and receiver Caleb Douglas also sat out. Because it was a bye-week session, some absences may have been precautionary. The Jets' Friday report belongs to their Week 6 game, not the Miami matchup. Breece Hall, guard Dylan Parham, receiver Adonai Mitchell and edge rusher Joseph Ossai were listed out after missing practice with injuries. Safety Dane Belton and tight end Kenyon Sadiq carried questions, while Omar Cooper Jr. entered a return window from injured reserve. Whatever happens in New York's game this weekend will become the starting point for its Miami report. The matchup implications are significant. If Savaiinaea cannot return, Jarrett Kingston is the likely replacement against a Jets defense with 17 sacks. If Brents, Taylor or Duck remain unavailable, Miami will again ask young defensive backs to cover Garrett Wilson. If Hall's quadriceps injury lingers, Braelon Allen would become New York's primary runner. away.headline: Dolphins have 12 players on their first Week 7 injury report
away.blurb: Running back Jaylen Wright (foot), safety Kyle Louis (knee), tight end Will Kacmarek (hamstring), wide receiver Caleb Douglas (ankle), long snapper Tucker Addington (shoulder) and defensive end Robert Beal Jr. (hamstring) were all limited. On Wednesday, Miami held their first official practice of the week at their Baptist Health Training Complex in preparation for this division battle. They also released their first injury report of the week, which included 12 players. The Dolphins listed cornerback Reese Taylor (quad) as the only non-participant. Full participants included quarterback Malik Willis (right thumb), linebacker Jordyn Brooks (foot), right guard Jonah Savaiinaea (ankle), cornerback JuJu Brents (heel) and linebacker Jackson Woodard (ankle). away.headline: Dolphins’ Caleb Douglas cleared to return from ankle injury against Jets
away.blurb: Douglas suffered the ankle ailment in the Sept. 20 loss to the San Francisco 49ers. He returned to practice this week and has been limited in drills Wednesday and Thursday before Friday’s session. After linebacker Willie Gay Jr. popped up on the Thursday injury report due to illness, Hafley said he’s back in the building Friday and feeling better. Gay participated in practice and is deemed questionable to play. The Dolphins have defensive end Rob Beal Jr., who has been back at practice through his hamstring injury, doubtful. Cornerback Reese Taylor, who has hurt quadriceps, is out. Taylor, at least, was seen participating in team stretch and then running and cutting on the side of practice, but he was still deemed a non-participant in practice. Rookie safety Kyle Louis, as he returned to practice this week, appears to be a Saturday decision on whether he is activated off injured reserve with the knee issue suffered in the opener against the Raiders. Listed as questionable, he is at least in play to return. For the Jets, coach Aaron Glenn told reporters Friday running back Breece Hall will be questionable, which held true at the release of the injury report. Hafley said he expects Hall to play after the standout rusher missed three games and he's preparing as such. New York has linebacker and Miami Hurricanes alum Kiko Mauigoa (quadriceps), offensive lineman Max Mitchell (concussion), edge rusher Joseph Ossai (ankle) ruled out. Questionable, along with Hall, are running back Kene Nwangwu (knee) and offensive lineman Dylan Parham (knee). Florida & Caribbean Experiences Florida Jewish Journal Florida Jewish Journal Branded Content Paid Partner Content MIAMI GARDENS — Miami Dolphins wide receiver Caleb Douglas is cleared to play in the upcoming game against the New York Jets on Sunday. Before Friday’s practice, Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley said Douglas will be good to go after missing three games with an ankle injury. The team’s injury report listed Douglas free of any game status designation after he underwent a full practice session. On Friday, Douglas appeared to be moving well running routes on air and catching passes from quarterback Malik Willis . “He's made a bunch of plays in practice,” said Hafley, who noted Douglas had taken part in individual and team portions of practice before Friday. “I'm excited to see him play. He hadn't played in a while. … It brings us some extra juice.” Without him, the Miami passing offense ranks 31st among 32 teams in the league on the year. The 6-foot-4 target who led the team with 94 receiving yards in the team’s opener against the Las Vegas Raiders could provide a boost to the passing game. Hafley also said running back Jaylen Wright, who has been dealing with a nagging foot injury, will play. The Bucs may or may not get Baker Mayfield back for this contest, but it will be a heated rivalry game regardless. It will also be crucial for the Buccaneers to cut into Carolina's division lead, so it could be a tough game regardless of how the two teams are perceived right now. What are the experts saying? CBS Sports analyst Pete Prisco has not once picked the Panthers to win, and they've proved him wrong thrice. This time, though, he's going with the surging Panthers, although he's still not predicting a big performance. Prisco picked a one-point Panthers win, saying, "The Bucs might have Baker Mayfield back for this one. That would be big. The Panthers are rolling on offense as Bryce Young is in the MVP conversation. It will stay that way, but the Bucs will hang around." His CBS colleague John Breech is also picking the Panthers, but he's taking them by a field goal. Arizona Republic's Jeremy Cluff is picking a Panthers win, 24-16, betting on the Bryce Young-led offense to continue clicking at home. SI's Ian MacMillan isn't buying any of what the Panthers are doing, and he's picking the Buccaneers to upset them in Charlotte. "Time to sell high on [the Panthers]. Their offense has been phenomenal to start the year, but I have plenty of questions surrounding the ability of some of the defenses they've had to face... I wouldn't be surprised to see them significantly regress. It could start this weekend when they take on a Tampa Bay defense that's fourth in opponent EPA per play and eighth in opponent success rate," he wrote. Here's how the rest of the SI staff is predicting this one: Mike Kadlick: Panthers Gilberto Manzano: Panthers John Pluym: Panthers Matt Verderame: Panthers Peter Dewey: Panthers Sporting News' Vinnie Iyer disagrees, predicting a 24-17 win. away.headline: Buccaneers Lose Three Key Starters for Week 7
away.blurb: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers will be without three important starters for their Week 7 matchup . The team officially ruled out wide receiver Emeka Egbuka, offensive tackle Luke Goedeke and safety Antoine Winfield Jr. Their absences leave Tampa Bay without a leading receiving threat, a starting offensive tackle and a key defensive contributor. With Winfield and Egbuka unavailable alongside Goedeke, Tampa Bay faces another challenging week managing key absences. Their availability will remain an important storyline as the Buccaneers prepare for Sunday’s matchup. The Tampa Bay Buccaneers expect Baker Mayfield to return as their starting quarterback Sunday against the Carolina Panthers . Mayfield missed three games after dislocating his right thumb during Tampa Bay’s Week 3 loss to Minnesota. Head coach Todd Bowles indicated Friday that Mayfield appeared ready after completing a full week of practice. Despite being listed as questionable, the veteran quarterback is expected to reclaim his starting role. Mayfield’s return follows three full practices while wearing a specially reinforced glove on his throwing hand. The device features a solid plate along the back to help prevent his previously dislocated thumb from bending backward. Although the glove changes how he grips the football, Mayfield believes he can compete. Mayfield had hoped to return for last week’s matchup against Pittsburgh. However, the Buccaneers gave him additional recovery time before he returned to game action. Tampa Bay eventually lost 26-19 in overtime after surrendering a fourth-quarter lead. Mayfield’s anticipated return comes as Tampa Bay looks to regain offensive consistency. Before suffering the injury, he threw for 615 yards, two touchdowns and two interceptions across three games. His absence put rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels in the starting lineup for the next three contests. Mayfield’s expected return provides Tampa Bay with an experienced leader after three games without him. Now, the Buccaneers will look to their veteran quarterback to spark the offense and help them get back on track against Carolina. Entertainment Entertainment Home ··· Boxing Winfield’s absence continues a frustrating stretch for the veteran safety. Rick Stroud previously reported that Winfield was expected to miss two to four weeks with a rib fracture. He has now missed two games while recovering from the injury. Emeka Egbuka’s Rookie Contract and Production Egbuka, 24, committed to Ohio State as a five-star recruit. He earned second-team All-Big Ten honors in 2022 before receiving third-team recognition in each of the following two seasons. Tampa Bay selected Egbuka 19th overall in the first round of the 2025 NFL Draft. He is playing the second season of a four-year, $18,147,572 contract, including a $9,838,231 signing bonus. The deal also includes a fifth-year option the Buccaneers can exercise in 2028. Through six games in 2026, Egbuka has recorded 28 receptions on 49 targets

He remained listed as questionable despite practicing fully all three days this week. “Maybe wait 1 more week? We’re inventing new glove technology so that he can return early with an injured throwing thumb to a 1-5 team?” the fan wrote . The team’s practice reports provide some encouraging evidence for the return. Fans remain concerned about how those throws will translate once Carolina’s defense gets involved. The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are preparing to get their starting quarterback back against the Carolina Panthers on Sunday. According to the Buccaneers’ account of his preparation , it provides support to prevent the injured ligament from bending backward. Mayfield also acknowledged adjusting his release points because the glove changes his grip. That detail prompted one fan to question the urgency. Another supporter made a similar argument using Tampa Bay’s record. “Its easier to rest him another week we are 1 and [expletive] 5 theres genuinely no rush if he’s not 100%,” the supporter wrote . The same user later clarified the criticism. “You’ve got me all wrong here, I agree he is hurt, the ‘gimmick’ is he always plays through injuries and it always goes horribly wrong,” the commenter added . home.headline: Jaelan Phillips is out, but his injury isn’t the only puzzle Panthers have to solve
home.blurb: Canales soon clarified that Phillips will be out for Sunday’s game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers: “I know there are advantages to game plans, but this is something that we need to address and take care of.” With Phillips officially out — it’s unclear if he’ll be ready by the Panthers’ Thursday Night Football game against the Packers in Week 8 — the Panthers are missing more than a run-of-the-mill defensive starter. The 27-year-old who the Panthers signed to a four-year, $120 million contract this free agency has lived up to his billing as a premier pass rusher; he has 2.5 sacks through five games but has also added 18 total pressures in the pass rush — 24th among all edge rushers , according to Pro Football Focus. Phillips has also been stout against the run and a vocal leader his teammates praise. What’s also a result of Phillips being out? The absence of Phillips comes at the same time as reserve outside linebacker and special teams ace Thomas Incoom is also “week to week” with a calf injury. Incoom exited the Eagles in the first half and didn’t return, and as a result the Panthers needed to do a whole bunch of roster magic to fill his role on special teams. In each of the four special teams units Incoom contributes on — kick return, kick coverage, punt return, punt coverage — the Panthers needed to replace him with four different players, Canales said. Canales was asked if the Panthers will elevate anyone from the practice squad with Phillips and Incoom out, and he indicated that Nick Hampton would. The interior offensive lineman was placed on the team’s injured reserve before the season began due to a hamstring injury and is now waiting for his 21-day practice window to be activated. When asked Wednesday, Canales was vague about Christensen’s situation: “We’re just evaluating it, and you gotta figure out roster spots as well,” before adding that he has faith in the team’s current slate of IOLs. If Christensen were to return, that limits their flexibility to use the injured reserve. It’s also worth noting the Panthers have already waived someone off the injured reserve with an injury settlement — Claudin Cherelus a few weeks ago — to avoid further limitations. It’s possible, perhaps likely, that once Cherelus gets healthy, he’d re-sign with the Panthers, rejoining the squad without forcing the team to use one of its eight precious IR-elevation moves. Ravens head coach Jesse Minter said that Jackson could "potentially" practice this week after missing all three of the team's practices ahead of Week 6. There have been reports the last two weeks that Jackson has a chance to play through his ankle injury, but he has not suited up in practice -- or for a game -- since Week 4. Minter: Lamar Jackson (ankle) could "potentially" practice this week. Remains day-to-day. Minter's update on Jackson isn't viewed as a positive one in the betting market. Ahead of Week 7, oddsmakers set the Ravens as three-point favorites at home in their matchup with the Bengals. He did combine for three scores in the win over Atlanta, so there is a higher ceiling that what he showed this past Sunday. If Jackson doesn't practice on Wednesday, it's possible this line could move even further towards the Bengals. For now, oddsmakers are still giving the Ravens the edge in this divisional battle. However, Jackson was not spotted at the beginning of practice and was later seen walking off with a limp. As a result, oddsmakers at DraftKings quickly shifted the odds in this game to Bengals -1.5, a huge 4.5-point flip from where they were entering the week. Lamar Jackson (ankle) seen walking off practice field with a limp, per @CordellWoodland . https://t.co/1R708hsFHo That's a sign that Jackson isn't expected to play in Week 7, and he may need to log a full practice on Thursday or Friday to shift the sentiment in the betting market. Sports Illustrated spoke to multiple oddsmakers this week about how they set the line for a game like this with Jackson's status up in the air. "Your lookahead line, you essentially have to assume he's going to play until you hear otherwise.," Ty Gour, Sports Trader at Fanatics Sportsbook, told Sports Illustrated. "So, that's baked into the price, whether we anticipate he'll be at full strength or 80% strength, that would kind of be factored in there. "And then, as the week goes on, we'll adjust as we know more. Obviously, he wasn't at practice today, and our line went down a point and a half just off that alone. And then we'll kind of trickle down as the week goes on and his status becomes more and more certain one way or the other. If he's back at practice tomorrow in a limited or full capacity, the line will probably shift back towards the Ravens. If he's not there again on Thursday, we'll essentially start pricing as though [Tyler] Huntley is going to be the starter." So, what could the line close at if Huntley makes his third start in a row? "If he's out and it's Huntley again, the line will most likely shift to the Bengals being the favorite, probably in that 1.5 to 2.5 range," Gour said. So, based on Gour's projection, the current line suggest that Jackson won't play. That would be a huge blow to a Ravens team that is 4-2 and already lost a division game in Week 6. As for the Baltimore Ravens , their kicker is on notice. These teams meet in a Week 7 AFC North clash, and here are bold predictions for the contest. The Bengals (3-2) enter the game in last place in the division despite having a winning record. That's because the Ravens, Steelers, and surprising Browns all have a record of 4-2. It should be another battle for the Ravens and Bengals. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Joe Burrow will riddle the Ravens' defense for 3 TD passes When the Bengals are right, they are tough on offense. And they've been cooking this year, ranking No. 9 in the NFL in points per game. Burrow is connecting on 71.4% of his passes. He has 11 touchdown passes and three interceptions. Look for him to keep the momentum going this week. But Burrow needs to take care of the football, which Zac Taylor said would go a long way in helping the Bengals win, according to Cleveland.com. "The turnovers is what screams at you," Taylor said. "That leads into field position." And Taylor said Burrow and his teammates are ready for this matchup. "It's exciting," Taylor said. "I think our guys really get fired up for this game. Not that they don't get fired up for every game, but whenever we play in Baltimore in a road divisional game, it's a fun one to get up for, and our guys will be up for it." Bengals RB Chase Brown will score two TDs One of them will be on the receiving end of a pass from Burrow. Brown will have a nice day, despite being caught in a time share with Samaje Perine, according to The Athletic. "I think we'll continually assess how that touch share between (Perine) and Chase Brown should play out," Bengals offensive coordinator Pitcher told Geoff Hobson of Bengals.com. "Every game's different. What type of scheme we lean into is going to factor into that. Obviously, what we ran more of yesterday leans into what Samaje does well, which is get downhill and run through contact." The Bengals haven't forgotten about their ground game. "You strive for balance when it comes to run-pass," Pitcher said. "You're always wanting to be the most balanced and versatile version of yourselves. It's like those are high-level goals that you set out to attain. But never in any given situation are we going to let a high-level theoretical goal get in the way of what it means on Sunday to win a game and what is the feedback we're getting in a game on a given Sunday." Derrick Henry will rush for 80-plus yards and a TD Henry is still smarting from last week's fumble that led to the Ravens' loss to the Browns. He took blame for the game-changing turnover , according to ESPN. "I got to take care of the ball," he said. "There's no excuses for that. I got to be better. I put the team in harm's way. I sound like a broken record with this, but I got to go back to work on it. Can't put the team in that situation." Teammate Kyle Hamilton took up for Henry. "Obviously, he's Derrick Henry, Hall of Fame running back [who] wants to hold onto the ball," Hamilton said. "He knows that. He's his harshest critic, so I'm not going to say anything ill about it. He's put us in position to win a lot of games." All of this will motivate Henry for a big game against the Bengals Ravens WR Ja'Kobi Lane will catch 5 passes and score a TD Lane looked ready to roll against the Browns in his return from injury. And he should be able to carve out a significant role in Week 7. Lane looked great in training camp. The injury short-circuited his 2026 season. But now he's back in the mix. His overall stat line could be impacted if Tyler Huntley is still at quarterback. But if Jackson is back, this could be a breakout game for Lane. Who will win the game? The Bengals should be able to outscore the Ravens in this matchup. But the key factor is Jackson. If he's back, the Ravens have a much better chance of winning. But we will still roll with Burrow, Chase, and Tee Higgins having a big game, along with Brown doing his thing. One of his teammates is anticipating a great game from him. Joe Burrow looking forward to facing Trey Hendrickson Burrow has practiced against Hendrickson many a time over the years, but the two have never been opponents in a real game before. There's no confusion on what he's expecting from No. 91, now in purple instead of orange. "It'll be fun, it'll be fun," Burrow said of seeing Hendrickson rushing at him . "I got to practice with him for a long time, and I'm sure he's excited to hit me a little bit after not hitting me for so long. It'll be fun." Hendrickson experienced the best years of his career on the team Burrow quarterbacked. The two nearly won a Super Bowl together, and almost made it back to another one a year later. Those memories are now an afterthought with undeniably high stakes in this matchup. The Bengals would like to avoid an 0-2 start in AFC North play. A loss would also drop them back to .500 at 3-3 overall. The Ravens just lost to the Cleveland Browns, and a second straight divisional defeat would set them back as well. How effectively Burrow evades his former teammate may determine the outcome in this game. Simpson is expecting greatness in Hendrickson's first chance at revenge, but Cincinnati is also looking for validation in moving on from the four-time Pro Bowler. away.headline: Ravens’ Lamar Jackson practices again, raising hopes for return vs. Bengals
away.blurb: Both Jackson and backup quarterback Tyler Huntley met with the media on Friday afternoon at the Ravens’ Owings Mills practice facility. By rule, teams must make their starting quarterback available to reporters at least once during the week leading up to a game. Having both quarterbacks available, though, was highly unusual. Typically, Jackson meets with reporters every Wednesday during the season. But with his status in question because of an injury, Baltimore waited until Friday each of the past two weeks to rule him out and make Huntley available. Jackson was officially listed as questionable Friday, leaving open the possibility that he could return for Sunday’s pivotal AFC North showdown against the Cincinnati Bengals. He took the podium in shorts and a T-shirt, his left ankle still heavily taped, offering little certainty about what the next two days might bring. Jackson practiced for a third consecutive day Friday, again on a limited basis. On its own, that was encouraging. But practice participation and playing a full game are two different things, and Jackson made it clear that foot pain remains a significant obstacle. The Ravens are also clearly trying to give the Bengals something to think about. There’s also his $260 million contract, which runs through the 2027 season but carries a salary-cap hit of more than $84 million next year. The sides couldn’t hammer out a deal this offseason , so they must address it soon. “If I can just go out there and feel the pain a little bit, I can play,” he said. “But [if] I’m restricted and I can’t do what I do, I’m not helping nobody. If I can just go out there and just be a statue and be hit, that’s not helping my team at all. That’s just me. I feel like I’m being selfish, because it’s about me at that point, for me to go out there and be hurt.” Ravens sack leader Tavius Robinson ruled out for season with injury Ravens outside linebacker Tavius Robinson was ruled out for Sunday after suffering a season-ending pectoral injury . Safety Jaylinn Hawkins (knee) is also out for this week. Defensive tackle Broderick Washington (tackle) is questionable, while cornerback T.J. Tampa (knee) is doubtful as he continues his return from injured reserve. Will Lamar Jackson play? Or won’t he? “I’m heading in the right direction,” Jackson said in his first comments to reporters since suffering the injury midway through an Oct. 4 win over the Tennessee Titans. “I can’t call it right now. “I feel like the swelling went down a lot, but just the pain tolerance. I’m just trying to move how I move. If I can’t do that, I can’t help my team. I can’t put my team in a situation like that. I feel like I’m doing a disservice then. … I can walk. It’s just trying to run, and [I can’t] put too much pressure.” “Between Lamar and our staff and us, it’s gonna be a decision based on him and how he feels and how effective he can be,” coach Jesse Minter said. “He’s had a good couple days, but we’ll see how it goes over the next 48 hours.

away.headline: What's Lamar Jackson's status for Bengals-Ravens AFC North tilt?
away.blurb: Jackson, who missed each of Baltimore's last two games due to an ankle sprain, will be listed as "questionable" on Oct. 23, according to multiple reports on Ravens head coach Jesse Minter's news conference that day. His status on the injury report was still to be determined, Minter said, because he was limited but also able to get in some work. ESPN reported on Oct. 23 that Jackson was observed warming up at Ravens practice. Jackson was listed as "limited" during Ravens practices on Oct. 21 and Oct. 22. The Bengals have plenty of familiarity with Huntley, having seen him in action for all or part of three games. One of those was a 2023 AFC Wild Card playoff game − a memorable Cincinnati win for since-retired and local product Sam Hubbard grabbing the ball after it was knocked out of Huntley's hands around the Bengals' defensive goal line. The Ravens (4-2) host the Cincinnati Bengals (3-2) at M&T Bank Stadium on Oct. 25 in a key AFC North showdown. In Jackson's absence, longtime backup Tyler Huntley has filled in and posted a 1-1 record. With Huntley as a starter this month, the Ravens lost a road game against the Cleveland Browns 13-10 in Week 6. Prior to that, Huntley helped steer Baltimore to a 30-23 overtime win against the Atlanta Falcons. Hubbard then returned the ball 98 yards for the game-winning score. The Baltimore Ravens have received an encouraging update on Lamar Jackson ahead of Sunday's divisional showdown with the Cincinnati Bengals. The quarterback returned to the practice field as he works toward a potential comeback from an ankle injury. The Athletic's Jeff Zrebiec reported on X that "Lamar Jackson is again on practice field for Ravens". Baltimore's official social media account also shared a video of the quarterback at practice, offering another positive sign for the team. ESPN's Jamison Hensley provided further details: Jackson has missed Baltimore's last two games after injuring his left ankle on October 4 against the Tennessee Titans. The Ravens went 1-1 in his absence, beating the Atlanta Falcons before suffering a 13-10 loss to the Cleveland Browns. Before the injury, Jackson had helped Baltimore make a strong start to the season. His availability could have a major impact on Sunday's AFC North matchup, with the Ravens looking to strengthen their position in the division. Baltimore will need to assess his condition before making a final call.

The Lamar Jackson injury watch continued Friday for Baltimore Ravens fans, NFL followers and fantasy football players alike. Jackson has missed the last two games due to ankle injury, which he revealed on Friday was a high-ankle sprain . The two-time MVP returned to practice on Thursday, however, and was on the field again for Friday's session. The Ravens host the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday and Jackson said that he's " headed in the right direction " for the contest. The 29-year-old signal-caller added that the ailment has been a " very, very painful " injury, but he doesn't need to be at full strength to suit up. Baltimore is currently in a three-way tie atop the AFC North at 4-2, with the Bengals sitting at 3-2. The Cleveland Browns (4-2) face the Tennessee Titans on Sunday, while the Pittsburgh Steelers (4-2) will play the New Orleans Saints on Sunday in Paris . Jackson has battled numerous injuries in recent years, missing five games apiece during the 2021 and 2022 campaigns and four more contests last season. home.headline: Ravens’ Lamar Jackson practices again, raising hopes for return vs. Bengals
home.blurb: Both Jackson and backup quarterback Tyler Huntley met with the media on Friday afternoon at the Ravens’ Owings Mills practice facility. By rule, teams must make their starting quarterback available to reporters at least once during the week leading up to a game. Having both quarterbacks available, though, was highly unusual. Typically, Jackson meets with reporters every Wednesday during the season. But with his status in question because of an injury, Baltimore waited until Friday each of the past two weeks to rule him out and make Huntley available. Jackson was officially listed as questionable Friday, leaving open the possibility that he could return for Sunday’s pivotal AFC North showdown against the Cincinnati Bengals. He took the podium in shorts and a T-shirt, his left ankle still heavily taped, offering little certainty about what the next two days might bring. Jackson practiced for a third consecutive day Friday, again on a limited basis. On its own, that was encouraging. But practice participation and playing a full game are two different things, and Jackson made it clear that foot pain remains a significant obstacle. The Ravens are also clearly trying to give the Bengals something to think about. There’s also his $260 million contract, which runs through the 2027 season but carries a salary-cap hit of more than $84 million next year. The sides couldn’t hammer out a deal this offseason , so they must address it soon. “If I can just go out there and feel the pain a little bit, I can play,” he said. “But [if] I’m restricted and I can’t do what I do, I’m not helping nobody. If I can just go out there and just be a statue and be hit, that’s not helping my team at all. That’s just me. I feel like I’m being selfish, because it’s about me at that point, for me to go out there and be hurt.” Ravens sack leader Tavius Robinson ruled out for season with injury Ravens outside linebacker Tavius Robinson was ruled out for Sunday after suffering a season-ending pectoral injury . Safety Jaylinn Hawkins (knee) is also out for this week. Defensive tackle Broderick Washington (tackle) is questionable, while cornerback T.J. Tampa (knee) is doubtful as he continues his return from injured reserve. Will Lamar Jackson play? Or won’t he? “I’m heading in the right direction,” Jackson said in his first comments to reporters since suffering the injury midway through an Oct. 4 win over the Tennessee Titans. “I can’t call it right now. “I feel like the swelling went down a lot, but just the pain tolerance. I’m just trying to move how I move. If I can’t do that, I can’t help my team. I can’t put my team in a situation like that. I feel like I’m doing a disservice then. … I can walk. It’s just trying to run, and [I can’t] put too much pressure.” “Between Lamar and our staff and us, it’s gonna be a decision based on him and how he feels and how effective he can be,” coach Jesse Minter said. “He’s had a good couple days, but we’ll see how it goes over the next 48 hours.

home.headline: Lamar Jackson fries Ian Rapoport for lying, dark day for reporters — NFL world reacts as Ravens superstar refutes insider’s injury update
home.blurb: Jackson’s comments drew reactions from analysts and Ravens fans alike, with some pointing out how the original report may have shaped perceptions of his recovery. Jackson, who ranks No. 2 in the league with a PFN QB Impact Score of 88.3, is listed as questionable for Baltimore’s Week 7 matchup against the Cincinnati Bengals. Lamar Jackson has found himself at the center of an injury-report controversy, and the Baltimore Ravens quarterback isn’t staying quiet about it. Jackson is still working his way back from an ankle issue, but he recently pushed back against Ian Rapoport’s report about its severity, saying his own trainers gave him a different diagnosis. Lamar Jackson Challenges Ian Rapoport’s Injury Report Jackson injured his left ankle during Baltimore’s Oct. 4 win over the Tennessee Titans and missed the next two games. Rapoport had reported that the injury was neither a high-ankle nor a low-ankle sprain. Jackson, however, said the Ravens’ medical staff gave him a different diagnosis. When a reporter asked about the discrepancy, Jackson questioned Rapoport’s source while making it clear that he was going with what his own medical staff told him. “Rapoport said that? He part of the training staff?” Jackson asked. “So we can’t go off Ian Rapoport and his reporting. Somebody probably told him that too, though, so I can’t blame him. But nah, man, my staff told me it was a high-ankle sprain, so we’re going with what [head certified athletic trainer] Adrian [Dixon] told me.” Physical therapist Jeff Mueller said the situation showed how easily information can get lost or changed as it passes from sources to reporters and then to fans. He wrote on X , “Great reminder that telephone between (source) and NFL insider often relays wrong information, and then, we intake wrong information as audience. If it was initially reported as a high ankle sprain, no one would be surprised that Lamar Jackson has missed this much time.” SET YOUR LINEUPS: PFN’s Free Fantasy Start/Sit Optimizer Meanwhile, Ravens podcast host Samuel Njoku was fed up with the uncertainty surrounding the quarterback’s injuries, posting , “Always ‘misinformation and speculation’ when it comes to Lamar injuries.” Rob Pizzola saw Jackson’s response as a win for the medical staff and a tough moment for NFL reporters. John Harbaugh and his coaching staff are in for a long week with plenty of fixes and a good start to this season at stake. Bert Bainbridge The pick: Texans, 24, Giants 10 Here's why: Regardless of who's under center for the Giants, this is a brutal matchup on the road against one the best defenses and a red-hot Texans offense. Big Blue stays keeps it within reach, but never close enough as Houston takes the one by two touchdowns. The pick: Texans 27, Giants 13 Here's why: The NFC East is there for the taking but the Giants haven't seemed interested and the fact that it took more than five minutes for Big Blue to name J.J. McCarthy this week's starter at quarterback speaks volumes. The pick: Texans 23, Giants 16 Here's why: Inconsistency is causing the Giants to decline a bit lately, and it's bad timing to be making this trip to face a Texans team that is showing signs of improvement. The pick: Texans 31, Giants 17 Here's why: These Giants are hard to predict, but their loss to the Saints showed they could be coming back to reality. With the quarterback situation, they're not a very good team right now. Mike Dougherty The pick: Texans 28, Giants 20 Here's why: A feel-good start masked the problems that are now surfacing. It's pretty clear after last week, the Giants are exactly what most believed they would be this season, a work in progress. The pick: Texans 34, Giants 17 Here's why: The Texans are surging thanks to C.J. Stroud quietly playing some of the best football of any QB in the NFL. Houston's defense is not as strong as last season, but the Giants have major questions on offense with the starting quarterback and main option at running back still in flux. Expect a comfortable win for the home team. This article originally appeared on NorthJersey.com: NY Giants vs Texans expert picks and predictions for Week 7 game

away.headline: New York Giants' Chauncey Golston out for season with neck injury
away.source: USA TODAY Touchdown Wire on MSN
away.blurb: Golston, placed on injured reserve (IR) earlier this month, is confirmed out for the year. The 28-year-old was hurt during New York’s Week 4 win over the Arizona Cardinals and did not return. He finished the game with two tackles before exiting. The former third-round pick out of Iowa had carved out a meaningful role in his second season with the Giants after signing a three-year, $18 million deal as a free agent in 2025. He appeared in each of the team’s first four games, working as a rotational piece on both base downs and in pass-rush packages while lining up at multiple spots along the defensive front. This article originally appeared on Giants Wire: New York Giants' Chauncey Golston out for season with neck injury The New York Giants will be without defensive lineman Chauncey Golston for the rest of the 2026 season after he suffered a neck injury. Early indications pointed to a long-term issue. Although Golston sought a second opinion in hopes of a better outcome, he will not be activated from IR. Golston’s versatility stemmed from his time in Dallas, where he developed as a flexible edge and interior contributor. His absence further thins an already taxed defensive line group. The Giants have also lost linebacker Tremaine Edmunds to a growing list of season-ending injuries after he suffered a torn chest muscle. New York will now need remaining defensive linemen and recent roster additions to absorb a larger share of snaps as the team moves through the middle of its schedule.

away.headline: Report: Giants' Tremaine Edmunds out for season with shoulder injury
away.source: USA TODAY Touchdown Wire on MSN
away.blurb: The injury marks the latest setback for a Giants defense that has been forced to reshuffle personnel repeatedly. With Burns already sidelined and now Edmunds out, the linebacking corps faces significant challenges in maintaining its effectiveness down the stretch. This article originally appeared on Giants Wire: Report: Giants' Tremaine Edmunds out for season with shoulder injury The New York Giants received another devastating injury blow on Friday with news that linebacker Tremaine Edmunds suffered a season-ending shoulder injury, reports Dan Duggan of The Athletic . The news compounds an already dire situation for a team that has already lost quarterback Jaxson Dart and outside linebacker Brian Burns, along with several other contributors, for the remainder of the year. Edmunds, one of the Giants’ top free-agent additions, had been a constant presence on defense, logging every snap while helping ease rookie linebacker Arvell Reese into the NFL. Micah McFadden is expected to step into Edmunds’ role and start alongside Reese. Head coach John Harbaugh has previously indicated the Giants view themselves as having three starting inside linebackers, giving McFadden the opportunity to seize a larger role in the middle of the defense. Edmunds’ absence removes a veteran presence and a key communicator from a unit already stretched thin by injuries. His consistency had provided stability next to the developing Reese, and his loss forces the Giants to lean more heavily on younger or less-proven options as they navigate the second half of the season. McFadden’s ability to fill the void will be closely watched as the Giants attempt to manage the mounting absences and stay competitive.

away.headline: New York Giants' Shocking Injury News Just Changed Everything
away.blurb: This will also make New York a step slower in its front seven, which will not only affect the pass rush (Edmunds actually has a couple of sacks this season), but also its pass coverage, which was already questionable. New York Giants' Shocking Injury News Just Changed Everything - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL F1 United States GP 2026 – Practice 3 TRENDING College football updates New York Giants' Shocking Injury News Just Changed Everything (Sam Navarro-Imagn Images) Matthew Schmidt Sat, October 24, 2026 at 11:00 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads As if the New York Giants didn't already have enough injuries, they just lost yet another key players for the year, as linebacker Tremaine Edmunds has gone down with a season-ending shoulder injury. Edmunds popped up on the injury report this week with the shoulder issue, but it didn't appear to be too big of a deal. Evidently, it was more serious than initially anticipated. Now, the Giants have lost the anchor of their linebacking corps, the man they signed to a three-year, $36 million contract in free agency back in March. New York's run defense was already struggling as it was, so to subtract Edmunds on top of that will make things that much more challenging for Big Blue. Micah McFadden will now step back into a starting role, and fortunately, he has long proven to be serviceable — but he is a definitive downgrade from Edmunds. This injury changes absolutely everything for the Giants. Edmunds' absence will now put that much more pressure on rookie Arvell Reese, and it also means that Reese's mentor will no longer be on the field with him. Reese has looked spectacular in certain moments this year, but he has also looked very much like a first-year player at other times, so losing Edmunds will unquestionably have an effect on the youngster. And of course, it will also give running backs yet even more of a chance to break through the Giants' linebacking corps and into the defensive backfield. New York has now lost two of its top defensive players in Edmunds and Brian Burns, which is beyond devastating for a unit that displayed so much potential during the season opener. The Giants are now incredibly thin on that side of the ball, and in an NFC East that is totally up for grabs, New York may slowly be losing its advantage. To make matters worse, the schedule is about to get tougher. The Giants will face the suddenly hot Houston Texans on the road on Sunday before heading into their bye week. Then, New York will begin a difficult stretch that runs all the way through Week 18. Even in such a horrendous division, it's becoming harder and harder to view the Giants as a potential playoff team given all of their injuries. First, Jaxson Dart . Then Burns. Now Edmunds. It continues to snowball.

McFadden was a full-time starter for the Giants in 2023 and 2024. In Game 1 last season, McFadden suffered a foot injury that kept him out for the remainder of the season. He admitted that "without a doubt" it isn't easy to no longer have a starting role. "Whenever you're used to something, you've had a taste of the pie, I guess, and then you don't get to go out there and eat with your boys anymore, it's tough, but I think it's just about staying present," McFadden said. "This game is a week-to-week basis, and obviously I had a pretty upsetting first week last year, and I learned a lot through that process, though. In the Chicago Bears 30-24 win over the New England Patriots , they triumphed despite allowing one of the most unique "Hail Mary" touchdown passes in recent memory. Patriots quarterback Drake Maye's 48-yard checkdown touchdown pass to running back Rhamondre Stevenson was the only touchdown pass in the last 20 years in the final 10 seconds of a half, 40-plus yards from the end zone on a throw of 10 or fewer air yards, per CBS Sports Research. What other craziness could happen during the rest of the NFL's Week 7 lineup? Daniel Jones cuts through Brian Flores' No. 1 Vikings defense The Minnesota Vikings are 5-0, and it is very much on the strength of defensive coordinator Brian Flores' aggressive unit. They are an immovable object. Flores' defense leads the NFL in: Scoring defense (12.8 points per game allowed) Third down defense (22.2% third down conversion rate allowed) Red zone defense (27.3% red zone touchdown rate allowed) Goal-to-go defense (33.3% goal-to-go touchdown rate allowed) Completion percentage allowed (53.2%) Touchdown-to-interception ratio allowed (3-6) Sack rate (9.8%) Pressure rate (46.4%) Blitz rate (69.8%) The Vikings' blitz rate of just under 70% (69.8%) is the highest by any team in any five-game span in the last 10 seasons, per CBS Sports Research. So how is that going to go for Indianapolis Colts quarterback Daniel Jones in Week 7? Well, the bold prediction here is that he doesn't commit any turnovers and totals multiple touchdowns against Flores' unit. Jones' splits versus the blitz are the exact same in terms of yards per pass attempt this season (5.9), and he actually has a higher completion percentage, touchdown-to-interception ratio, and passer rating against the blitz in 2026. Jones also got to spend the second half of the 2024 season watching how Flores' unit operates up close in practice on a daily basis after Minnesota scooped him up for depth purposes after his New York Giants release. That practice experience against Flores will allow Jones to produce a clean, efficient performance. Daniel Jones vs. the blitz, 2026 season Pass attempts Completion percentage Pass yards per attempt Air yards per attempt Passer rating Bijan Robinson goes runs wild vs. the undefeated 49ers The undefeated San Francisco 49ers not only have a top-five scoring offense (29.5 points per game) but also a top-10 scoring defense (18.3 points allowed per game). That also extends to their run defense, which ranks as the seventh-best in football, allowing just 90.2 rushing yards per game. Bijan Robinson , who enters Week 7 leading the NFL with 785 yards from scrimmage, will go off for 150-plus rushing yards against San Francisco. He'll be well rested after having just 11 touches in Week 6, his fewest in a game since 2024, and Robinson will break what has been one of the 49ers' biggest strengths: their control of outside-zone runs. San Francisco has curbed outside-zone runs to just 3.2 yards per carry, the sixth-fewest in the NFL, and they are the only defense that hasn't allowed a gain of 10 or more yards on those runs, per the NFL's Next Gen Stats. They have also tackled rushers for a loss or no gain on 5 of 29 outside-zone carries, 17.2%. Robinson has 10 explosive runs (gains of 10 or more yards) on his 65 outside-zone carries, tied with Derrick Henry for the most in the league. He's also only been stuffed for no gain or a loss on 6 of his 65 outside-zone run carries. Robinson will repeatedly cook the 49ers, rushing to the outside, and he'll become not only the first player with over 100 yards rushing against San Francisco in 2026 but the first player to hit at least 150 yards rushing against San Francisco. Cardinals stun Broncos without scoring a touchdown The Arizona Cardinals (2-4) upset the preseason Super Bowl favorite Los Angeles Rams 18-16 in Week 6 as 13.5-point road underdogs, earning the second-largest upset win by any team in the last five seasons, according to CBS Sports Research. They accomplished that feat despite not finding the end zone one time. Arizona's 18 points came from six made field goals. The Cardinals host the Denver Broncos (4-2) while seeking their first win away from SoFi Stadium -- both of Arizona's wins have come on the road against the Rams and the Los Angeles Chargers . Denver enters Week 7 with a top 10 scoring defense (20.8 points per game, 10th in the NFL), but Arizona will upset them too for their first home win of the season. Even more impressively, the Cardinals will also beat the Broncos without scoring a touchdown, just like they did with the Rams in Week 6. How will that work? Arizona will pull off that near-impossibility thanks to the Broncos' offensive ceiling being capped by starting quarterback Bo Nix . Nix's 5.6 yards per pass attempt are the fewest in the NFL among quarterbacks to start every game in 2026, and his 4.9 air yards per pass attempt represent the shortest average pass length through six games in the last 20 seasons, according to CBS Sports Research. Not having to defend the deep ball will allow the Cardinals to get creatively aggressive on defense, and Nix will give Arizona's similarly shaky offense, led by journeyman Jacoby Brissett, enough latitude to win with six or seven made field goals and no touchdowns. J.J. McCarthy avoids being sacked vs. Will Anderson Jr., Texans The New York Giants have a new starting quarterback for Week 7 at the Houston Texans : Minnesota Vikings' 2024 10th overall pick castoff J.J. McCarthy . He ranked dead last in the NFL in completion percentage (57.6%), touchdown-to-interception ratio (11-12) and passer rating (72.6) among 33 qualified quarterbacks in 2025. He also had a 10% sack rate last season, the third highest in the entire league. However, McCarthy will not be sacked in his debut as the Giants' starting quarterback despite facing the Houston Texans and All-Pro edge rusher Will Anderson Jr. , the NFL's sacks leader with 7.5 entering Week 7. How will that happen? Perhaps McCarthy has taken a big leap from 2025 to 2026. After checking in for a benched Jameis Winston in the fourth quarter in Week 6, McCarthy threw for 243 yards, the most by any quarterback in the play-by-play era (since 1991) who had no passing yards in the first three quarters, per CBS Sports Research. The humbling he took, being traded for a 2027 fifth-round pick, plus playing in a more simplistic offense in New York under offensive coordinator Matt Nagy and senior offensive assistant Greg Roman, will allow McCarthy to play a cleaner game in Week 7. That will help him avoid Anderson Jr. and Danielle Hunter's clutches as he avoids being sacked all game long. Dolphins take a lead for the first time this season The Miami Dolphins ' 2026 season is going exactly as one would expect for a franchise paying more for players not on its roster (an NFL-record $179 million in dead cap hits) than for the players on its roster ($156 million). They're 0-5 and have the NFL's worst scoring offense, averaging 14 points per game. They're also just the second team in the Super Bowl era (since 1966) to not have a lead in the first five games of a season, along with the 2005 Houston Texans, per CBS Sports Research. However, they will acquire their first lead in a game of the 2026 season against the New York Jets . The Jets have the worst red zone offense (37.5%) in the NFL, and they haven't scored a touchdown on their last seven red zone trips, which spans the last three games. New York has also been outscored 100-6 in the final two minutes of the first half under Aaron Glenn. Miami will capitalize on Glenn's end-of-the-first-half mismanagement and take a lead in a game for the first time this season. Meanwhile, the Arizona Cardinals may be 2-4, but they're coming off a huge divisional victory over the Los Angeles Rams. The Cardinals are feeling it right now, and they're at home — but we know how Broncos Country travels, especially in the desert. At 4-2, the Broncos can't afford a slip-up — not if they want to keep pace with the Kansas City Chiefs in the division, and make their Week 8 rematch at Mile High a potential chance to get back to the top of the division, depending on what happens this Sunday with the Seattle Seahawks. That's me looking past the Cardinals a little bit. The Broncos won't be doing that. Sean Payton knows how to keep a team's focus on whichever game and opponent is up next, and that's the Cardinals. How will this one shake out? Let's go around the table to see how the Denver Broncos On SI / Mile High Huddle staff see Sunday's action unfolding in Glendale, AZ. All the internal tinkering on Nix might not be as important as facing a Cardinals team the Broncos should beat. While most eyes will be focused on how Nix performs, it's returning rookie running back Jonah Coleman who steals the limelight with two scores. Looking at the Cardinals' 31st-ranked scoring defense — a unit allowing 350.5 yards per game — this is about as golden a get-right opportunity Nix could hope for. Courtland Sutton said , "At some point, the tide's going to turn" for Nix and this offense, and it happens at State Farm Stadium on Sunday. Nix passes for three touchdowns and 280 yards, while the Broncos romp in the desert. If not now for Nix, then when? Go out there and dominate, and those “confidence issues” will miraculously disappear. I foresee a better showing, though maybe not quite the 2018 Kick Your A** blowout. Nix has been a shell of himself through six weeks in the 2026 season, yet Denver is somehow 4-2 and favored on the road against the Arizona Cardinals in Week 7. Arizona is coming off a massive upset win on the road against the Los Angeles Rams, and while it may not be a playoff team, the Cardinals are not a pushover this season. Jacoby Brissett and Co. will have their work cut out for them against a Denver defense that is one of the best in the NFL. The Bronco offense (29th in success rate) hasn’t been able to get much going during this 4-2 start, but the defense has forced 10 turnovers and is allowing just 5.0 yards per play. The play on that side of the ball has stayed intact even with Pat Surtain II (missed the last two games) and Talanoa Hufanga (missed Week 6) injured. Arizona’s defense is one of the weaker ones that the Broncos have on the schedule, so Sean Payton may look to get his young quarterback going early on Sunday. Will it lead to a Denver win? All season long, the SI Betting team is sharing final score predictions for every NFL game, and we’re hoping it’ll help our readers decide on some spread, moneyline and total bets along the way. Plus, who doesn’t want to get an exact score bet right during the season? Denver is favored on the road, but can bettors trust this offense with Nix struggling? This spread suggests we could see a close game, so let’s dive right into my score prediction for this Week 7 battle. Broncos vs. Cardinals Odds, Spread and Total Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook Broncos -4.5 (-110) Cardinals +4.5 (-110) Broncos: -230 Cardinals: +190 43.5 (Over -115/Under -105) This line has held steady since it opened , as the Broncos are still favored on the road by 4.5 points despite Arizona’s win over the Rams in Week 6. Broncos vs. Cardinals Score Prediction This week, SI Betting’s Iain MacMillan continued his quest to bet on every NFL game in his Road to 272 column . In this matchup, he’s taking Denver to win and cover despite some early struggles on offense: You can throw all of the Broncos' middling metrics out the window, because no team has had a tougher schedule to begin the season than Denver. They've faced the Chiefs, Jaguars, Rams, 49ers, Chargers, and Seahawks, and came out on the other end of that run with a 4-2 record. Despite playing that good a record, their defense still ranks sixth in opponent EPA per play and fifth in opponent success rate. Just imagine how good this defense is going to look when facing lower-tier competition. The Cardinals may be coming off the upset of the year over the Los Angeles Rams, but they enter this week ranking dead last in the NFL in net yards per play at -1.4. Their offense is solid at times, but their defense remains one of the worst units in the league. Give me the Broncos as road favorites. MacMillan has confidence in the Broncos this week, but I’m eyeing the UNDER with the Denver offense looking like one of the worst in the NFL. Arizona’s offense has been able to move the ball with Brissett under center, but Denver has been an elite defense the last few weeks, moving up into the top-12 in the league in points allowed, yards per play allowed, EPA/Play and success rate. The Cardinals are ninth in success rate and 15th in EPA/Play on offense, yet they’ve still scored 21 or fewer points in three of their six games. I expect Brissett to have a much tougher time against a Denver pass defense that – without Pat Surtain II – dominated Seattle and Los Angeles in back-to-back weeks. On the other side of the ball, how can anyone bet on Denver to put up points? The UNDER has hit in five of the Broncos’ six games this season, partially due to the fact that they’ve scored 23 or fewer points in five games and 20 or fewer points in four games. away.blurb: Denver Broncos cornerback Pat Surtain went down with a non-contact ankle injury late in the second quarter of Sunday's game against the San Francisco 49ers . Broncos CB Pat Surtain questionable for Week 7 Denver's injury report for Sunday's game against Arizona has cornerback Pat Surtain officially listed as questionable . If he can't play, Jahdae Barron will likely be the next man up. Despite returning to practice on Wednesday, Pat Surtain seems more likely to return in Week 8 against the Chiefs, according to James Palmer of NFL on Prime Video . We'll see how the week goes for PS2. Pat Surtain might not return in Week 7 In an updated report on Pat Surtain's status, James Palmer of Prime Video clarified that PS2's injury was not a non-contact injury — it actually happened one play before the cornerback went down on the field. Palmer also reported that " [i]t might be tough " for Surtain to return to action in Week 7, suggesting PS2 might be more likely to return in Week 8. Pat Surtain ruled out for Week 6; there's hope for possible Week 7 return Pat Surtain has been ruled out for a Thursday Night Football clash with the Seattle Seahawks in Week 6, but there is hope he might be able to return against the Arizona Cardinals in Week 7, according to KUSA-TV's Mike Klis . Pat Surtain avoids IR; ruled out for Week 5 ESPN's Adam Schefter said on Altitude Sports Radio that his guess is that Pat Surtain will land on injured reserve , which would rule the cornerback out for at least four games. NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported this morning that Pat Surtain is expected to miss time, but it's not believed to be season-ending. "You hope it is just a couple weeks, maybe it ends up in an IR stint, but not expected to be season-ending," Rapoport said . Broncos CB Pat Surtain ruled out Broncos cornerbacks Pat Surtain (ankle) and Riley Moss (ribs), who were both originally listed as questionable to return, have been announced as ruled out for the rest of today's game. Riley Moss and Jahdae Barron are the two outside cornerbacks with Ja'Quan McMillian playing in the slot. Behind them on Denver's depth chart , the Broncos also have Kris Abrams-Draine. With PS2 sidelined, the team is down to four healthy cornerbacks on the active roster. Update : Moss (ribs) was announced as questionable to return after halftime, so Denver now has Barron and Abrams-Draine starting at the two outside cornerback spots. Surtain was down on the field for a few moments before being helped off by two people, walking slowly into the locker room. away.headline: Cardinals get troubling Jeremiyah Love injury update before Broncos game
away.blurb: Arizona held Love out of last week’s matchup against the Los Angeles Rams, giving the rookie additional time to recover from his ankle injury. For Love, the priority remains getting healthy enough to return without risking another setback. While Arizona has not officially ruled him out for Sunday, the latest report suggests the team may need to prepare for another game without one of its most important young offensive players. Giants DC Threatens Players Amid 'Unacceptable' Behavior, Calls Out 'Traitors' The Arizona Cardinals could be without one of their most promising offensive weapons for another week. Rookie running back Jeremiyah Love is expected to miss Sunday’s matchup against the Denver Broncos as he continues recovering from an ankle injury, according to CBS Sports’ Matt Zenitz. Love already missed Arizona ‘s Week 6 victory over the Los Angeles Rams, and the latest report suggests the Cardinals could be forced to play without their starting running back for a second consecutive game. The former Notre Dame standout did not participate in Wednesday’s practice, raising further concerns about his availability heading into Week 7. Love has been dealing with an ankle injury that initially surfaced following Arizona’s Week 4 matchup against the New York Giants. Although he returned to action against the Detroit Lions in Week 5, the rookie struggled to find his rhythm, finishing with just 22 rushing yards on 12 carries. Before being sidelined, Love had rushed for 245 yards and one touchdown on 67 carries through five games. He also contributed 11 receptions for 36 yards and another touchdown. Arizona selected Love with the third overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, making him the highest-drafted running back since Saquon Barkley went second overall in 2018. The Cardinals entered the season with high expectations for the former Fighting Irish star, who established himself as one of college football’s most explosive offensive players. Now, his early NFL career has been interrupted by injuries. With Love expected to remain sidelined, Arizona could once again turn to Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight to handle the rushing responsibilities. The Cardinals leaned on their running back depth during last week’s victory, but facing Denver presents another challenge for an offense attempting to establish consistency. The Cardinals have invested heavily in the rookie’s long-term future, and his availability will be an important storyline as the season progresses. But Nix was back and good to go for Week 1 of the 2026 NFL season. With a still-strong offense that added Jaylen Waddle and an elite defense, it seemed like the sky was the limit for the 2026 Broncos. But through six weeks, it's been far from ideal. home.headline: Cardinals get troubling Jeremiyah Love injury update before Broncos game
home.blurb: Arizona held Love out of last week’s matchup against the Los Angeles Rams, giving the rookie additional time to recover from his ankle injury. For Love, the priority remains getting healthy enough to return without risking another setback. While Arizona has not officially ruled him out for Sunday, the latest report suggests the team may need to prepare for another game without one of its most important young offensive players. Giants DC Threatens Players Amid 'Unacceptable' Behavior, Calls Out 'Traitors' The Arizona Cardinals could be without one of their most promising offensive weapons for another week. Rookie running back Jeremiyah Love is expected to miss Sunday’s matchup against the Denver Broncos as he continues recovering from an ankle injury, according to CBS Sports’ Matt Zenitz. Love already missed Arizona ‘s Week 6 victory over the Los Angeles Rams, and the latest report suggests the Cardinals could be forced to play without their starting running back for a second consecutive game. The former Notre Dame standout did not participate in Wednesday’s practice, raising further concerns about his availability heading into Week 7. Love has been dealing with an ankle injury that initially surfaced following Arizona’s Week 4 matchup against the New York Giants. Although he returned to action against the Detroit Lions in Week 5, the rookie struggled to find his rhythm, finishing with just 22 rushing yards on 12 carries. Before being sidelined, Love had rushed for 245 yards and one touchdown on 67 carries through five games. He also contributed 11 receptions for 36 yards and another touchdown. Arizona selected Love with the third overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, making him the highest-drafted running back since Saquon Barkley went second overall in 2018. The Cardinals entered the season with high expectations for the former Fighting Irish star, who established himself as one of college football’s most explosive offensive players. Now, his early NFL career has been interrupted by injuries. With Love expected to remain sidelined, Arizona could once again turn to Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight to handle the rushing responsibilities. The Cardinals leaned on their running back depth during last week’s victory, but facing Denver presents another challenge for an offense attempting to establish consistency. The Cardinals have invested heavily in the rookie’s long-term future, and his availability will be an important storyline as the season progresses.
