home.blurb: Head coach Mike LaFleur announced the news in his press conference on Friday, Oct. 23, ahead of the Cardinals' game against the Denver Broncos. This marks the second consecutive game that Love has missed as the Cardinals, following a nagging ankle injury that limited his explosiveness in recent weeks. In addition to Love, LaFleur ruled out defensive tackle Walter Nolen, safety Andrew Wingard and right guard Jon Gaines. Nolen, the Cardinals’ 2025 first-round pick, injured his ankle in the third quarter of last week’s win over the Rams . He returned to the game but came up limping after a snap late in the fourth quarter and did not return. Gaines is the newest addition to the injury report, as he suffered an ankle injury in practice on Thursday, Oct. 22. “Enough to keep him out for this week,” LaFleur said. The same goes for defensive lineman Darius Robinson, who was downgraded to questionable with a back injury on Thursday. LaFleur said that the situation is “similar” with cornerback Max Melton, who was limited on Wednesday and did not practice on Thursday due to a knee injury. When asked, LaFleur said the Cardinals have not discussed placing Love on injured reserve. In Love's absence, the Cardinals will once again turn to Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight to lead their backfield. In Week 6, Allgeier finished with 18 carries for 38 yards, while Knight took 15 carries for 80 yards. Both players saw two targets, while Allgeier led in snap share, 56% to 44%. LaFleur described Allgeier as more of the Cardinals’ third-down back, whereas Knight’s role is more on first and second downs. Last week, Allgeier played on 10 of 15 third downs. On first and second down, Allgeier had 29 snaps to Knight’s 26. “(Allgeier) is extremely smart, so he's very beneficial for us on third downs, with the protection schemes, with his firmness, in terms of picking up pressures,” LaFleur said. “… So he provides that skill set for us. He can still do what we need on first and second down, but that's where Bam ends up coming in and doing a lot of that work on first and second down.” LaFleur said that the Cardinals do not expect Nolen to be placed on injured reserve, but he left the door more open there than he did with Love. “Don't expect, but as I've learned through seven weeks of the job, I expect anything,” LaFleur said. “But I just answer it with him; he's no different than all the other guys. Not expecting it, but there are setbacks. These are human bodies.” Wingard, meanwhile, will miss his third consecutive game after suffering a knee injury against the Giants in Week 4. The Cardinals have multiple options to fill his void at safety, with Wydett Williams and Dadrion Taylor-Demerson both now healthy. They could also play cornerback Garrett Williams in that spot, as they did last week. The Cardinals will turn to 2025 sixth-round pick Hayden Conner in Gaines’ absence. Meanwhile, on the opposite side of the ball, Green Bay – led under center by sixth-year passer Jordan Love – has scored the 10th-fewest points in the game (21.2/game). Through six weeks, Love has also completed just 59.7 percent of his pass attempts. If the season ended today, it'd rank as his lowest completion percentage as a starting quarterback in the NFL. Yet, multiple Green Bay pass-catchers have flourished, most notably wide receivers Christian Watson and Matthew Golden. Watson, now in his fifth NFL season, has already amassed as many touchdowns as last season (six) and nearly as many receptions (29) and reception yards as he did a year ago (538). The former second-round pick secured 35 catches and 611 yards in 10 games a season ago. Meanwhile, Golden, Green Bay's first-round pick in 2025, has already surpassed all his receiving totals from his rookie campaign. He's already racked up 30 catches, 501 yards and three touchdowns amid a career breakout season. And just like Watson, he's well on pace for a 1,000-yard receiving campaign. Consequently, both Watson and Golden possess the potential to wreak havoc against the Lions’ secondary, even with Pro Bowl safety Brian Branch back in the fold for Detroit. In addition to Watson and Golden, the Lions will also likely have their hands full with Packers running back Josh Jacobs. The Pro Bowler returns to the lineup after spending the first six weeks of the season on the commissioner exempt list for an offseason domestic abuse incident. Jacobs, who's coming off a 929-yard, 13-touchdown rushing campaign in 2025, should provide an immediate boost to Green Bay's league-worst ground game. In case you were wondering, the Packers have compiled a measly 359 total rushing yards through the season's first six games. Expect Jacobs, along with Watson and Golden, to give Kelvin Sheppard's defense its fair share of fits on Sunday. However, at this present juncture, I'm still willing to give the Lions a 60 percent chance to pull off the Week 7 victory at home. Green Bay Packers edge rusher Micah Parsons was originally expected to make his 2026 season debut in Week 6 after his long journey from tearing his ACL and meniscus last year in Week 15. Packers coach Matt LaFleur told reporters on Monday that Parsons will not practice this week, meaning he won't be ready to go for Week 7's game versus the Detroit Lions , an NFC North rival for Green Bay. "He's got to clear some hurdles yet to get to that point," LaFleur said. The Packers will have to open Parsons's 21-day practice window before fans can even expect him to get close to playing. away.headline: Packers HC Matt LaFleur gets brutally honest on Josh Jacobs returning to Green Bay
away.blurb: Green Bay Packers head coach Matt LaFleur addressed Josh Jacobs’ return Wednesday, acknowledging the running back’s off-field legal troubles while expressing his belief in second chances. For now, the former Alabama standout is eligible to return, but his status for Sunday and potential league discipline remain unresolved. Jacobs returned to practice after missing Green Bay’s first six games while on the NFL’s Commissioner’s Exempt List. His reinstatement comes amid an ongoing league investigation into a domestic incident involving his former girlfriend. The 33rd Team’s Ari Meirov shared a video on X, formerly Twitter, showing LaFleur discussing how the Packers balance welcoming Jacobs back with the seriousness of his legal case. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The 2022 first-team All-Pro running back pleaded no contest to misdemeanor battery and criminal damage to property charges stemming from a May altercation with his then-girlfriend. The NFL placed Jacobs on the Commissioner’s Exempt List on August 30 before removing him on Monday. However, his removal does not conclude the NFL’s investigation under its Personal Conduct Policy. Additional discipline remains possible, and whether his six missed games will count toward a future suspension has not been finalized. Jacobs and the woman involved also filed a lawsuit seeking to prevent the release of evidence related to the incident. On the field, the Packers desperately need rushing production. Green Bay enters Sunday’s matchup vs. the Lions averaging an NFL-worst 59.8 rushing yards per game despite holding a 4-2 record and riding a three-game winning streak. Jacobs’ Week 7 availability remains uncertain , as LaFleur has not confirmed whether he will play. The Packers also have a temporary roster exemption for Jacobs that expires on October 26. The four questionable are guard Aaron Banks (knee/toe), cornerback Benjamin St-Juste (hamstring), receiver Bo Melton (back) and defensive tackle Jordon Riley (Achilles), who's currently on the physically unable to perform list and would need to be added to the 53-man roster to play against the Lions. picks.headline: Rams vs. Raiders bold predictions for NFL Week 7
picks.blurb: Rams vs. Raiders bold predictions for NFL Week 7 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football F1 United States GP 2026 – Practice 3 TRENDING College football updates NFL injury updates Brewers take Game 1 Tatum downplays beef Knicks change ring tune Rams vs. Raiders bold predictions for NFL Week 7 Kiyoshi Mio-Imagn Images Douglas Fritz, ClutchPoints Thu, October 22, 2026 at 6:41 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads There is a big time injury for the Los Angeles Rams . And the Raiders have a major concern as well. These teams meet in Week 7, and here are bold predictions for the NFL contest. It's a crucial game for the Rams, who stand at 2-4 and find themselves a staggering four games behind the front-running 49ers in the NFC West. Meanwhile, the Raiders stand at 3-3 in third place in the AFC West. They're unlikely to be a playoff contender, but are trying to build a strong foundation for 2027. Let's take a look at what could happen when these teams battle. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Matthew Stafford will throw for three touchdowns It's hard to gauge what kind of yardage output Stafford will have. Without the injured Davante Adams, the Rams may lean on the ground game a little more. Adams is the team's leading receiver with 480 yards and four touchdowns. Sure, Stafford still has Puka Nacua. And Nacua will get his targets and yardage. But who steps into the No. 2 role? Maybe the Rams will use tight end Tyler Higbee more. Or perhaps Konata Mumpfield or Jordan Whittington will step up and produce. However, despite the receiver situation, the Rams will need to find a way to get the ball into the end zone if the Raiders load up to stop the run in the red zone. So look for Stafford to spread it around and still get his TD passes. Stafford said he understands the situation , according to The Athletic. "I just feel even more responsibility to try to be as good as I can be to help us continue to win," Stafford said. "In some of those guys' instances where they're going to have opportunities to hopefully come back and play for us, make sure that when they come back and play for us, it's meaningful stuff for them." However, some observers think Stafford has finally reached the end of his NFL rope, according to ESPN. "Stafford can't move," Ben Solak wrote. "He was never the most mobile quarterback, but the Rams were willing to use him on boots in the past. In 2024, 16.8% of Stafford's pass attempts were on the run — an above-average number! That fell to 13.9% in 2025 and is down to 9.6% in 2026. Sure, designed rollouts are down — but it isn't just that. "Stafford has zero scrambling passing yards on the season per NFL Next Gen Stats. He has yet to break the pocket and complete a pass on a scramble drill. The last quarterback to log no scramble passing yards through six weeks of a season was 2022 Tom Brady — the final season of a pocket passing titan." But it's not time to write Stafford off. Rams RB Kyren Williams will rush for 90-plus yards The Rams must run the football against the Raiders, a team that struggles to stop the ground game. The Raiders are giving up 134.3 yards per game, which ranks No. 28 in the NFL. Keeping the ball on the ground needs to be a big part of the Rams' game plan. The Rams have thrown 252 passes with 148 rushing attempts. McVay wants those numbers closer together , according to theramswire.com. "Ultimately, what I care about and what we care about is what's the best way is to move the ball and score points," McVay said. "Because of some of the situations that we've been in, those two-minute situations have gotten us a little bit out of balance. No matter how I cut it, it's an excuse. I'd like to be able to have a little bit more balance. And that's reflected by being efficient on early downs and sustaining drives." One thing is for sure, Williams and the Rams haven't lost their belief that this can be a special season. "Man, my confidence is still as high as ever," Williams said. "We know what we've got on our team and in this locker room. We come to practice every single week. That's why we can't lose our focus. We can't lose what matters the most, and that's the work. "It's about having faith. That the work we put in every single week will come to shine." Raiders RB Ashton Jeanty will split carries with Mike Washington Jr. There's no doubt that Jeanty has been a huge disappointment for the Raiders. They picked him No. 6 overall, expecting a franchise-changing player. Instead, Jeanty has a career average of 3.5 yards per carry. And Washington has been turning heads with the coaching staff, according to a post on the Raiders' YouTube page via Athlon Sports. But he needs to be better at pass protection . "He's a rookie, so he had a lot to catch up on," Kubiak said when asked about Washington's role in the passing game. "He's continuing to improve. (And) he's putting the work in. You see the practice come to life in the games. He's not where he wants to be. He's got to keep growing." Jeanty has been a threat in the passing game. Maybe his future is as a third-down back. Washington could supplant him. And the prediction is for that to begin this week. Jeanty has time to bounce back. It's still early in his career. But he simply hasn't been able to show in the NFL what he showed in college. Or they were expected to be coming into the season. A vicious string of injuries have the Rams coming to town potentially looking a lot different at this point than originally expected. Which has the staff feeling pretty good about the Raiders' chances. I gathered up everyone's predictions for the game to see if there is any kind of consensus. Justin Melo -- Rams 27, Raiders 24 The Los Angeles Rams are banged up, but it's a back-against-the-wall moment for them. Matthew Stafford makes just enough plays for the Rams to escape with a 27-24 victory. Marvin Uzor -- Raiders 27, Rams 24 The Rams have struggled against the run, and I expect Ashton Jeanty to take advantage. That should take some pressure off Kirk Cousins and give the Raiders enough balance to snap their three-game losing streak at home. Lamarr Fields -- Raiders 28, Rams 24 I think Raiders will be able to run the ball better this week and get a few stops to beat the banged-up Rams on late 4th quarter touchdown Levi Damien -- Raiders 27, Rams 23 I see this as the perfect opportunity for the Raiders to pull out of their losing streak. Two of the three games in the streak were competitive games against tough opponents in the Chiefs and Bills. And both were at home. I had the Rams winning this one in my preseason predictions. But without the likes of Myles Garrett, Davante Adams, and the two injured DTs -- and possibly Puka Nacua and Trent McDuffie as well -- I think the door is open for the Raiders to get the win. Pick totals: Raiders 3, Rams 1 Average score: Raiders 27, Rams 25 Most of the staff sees this as a game the Raiders can edge out the Rams. With an average score differential of 3.67 points in those picks. If there is a consensus it's that everyone thinks this will be a close one with no prediction picking the game to be decided by more than a four-point margin. away.headline: Rams-Raiders injury report: Trent McDuffie, Nate Landman miss practice
away.source: USA TODAY Touchdown Wire on MSN
away.blurb: On Wednesday, Trent McDuffie and Nate Landman both missed practice. Landman is in the concussion protocol, while McDuffie is still recovering from a groin injury that caused him to sit out Week 6 against the Cardinals. Defensive tackle Tonka Hemingway was the only non-participant for the Raiders. Five other players were limited, including Brock Bowers and Kolton Miller. After dropping their last two games, the Los Angeles Rams are back to work in advance of their Week 7 matchup with the Las Vegas Raiders . The injury bug bit the Rams hard on Sunday, as Davante Adams, Kobie Turner, Poona Ford and Blake Grupe were all lost to IR, so Los Angeles will be shorthanded against Vegas this week. They won't make any excuses, though. Sean McVay said the Rams are monitoring McDuffie's progress to see if he'll be ready to go against the Raiders. McDuffie and Landman were the only players who did not participate in practice. Josh Wallace has a calf injury but was a full participant, as was Colby Parkinson (shoulder). away.headline: Rams get interesting trade report after Davante Adams' multi-week injury
away.blurb: After such a brutal injury, ESPN's Dan Graziano is reporting that the Rams, even at 2-4, are expected to search the WR trade market for potential additions to try and keep their season alive while Adams is out. It wouldn't make sense to give up now, especially since Garrett should come back, and Adams could return later this season as well. Rams get interesting trade report after Davante Adams' multi-week injury | Sporting News Skip to main content SN 140 Watch Watch How to Watch Streaming Services fubo Add Sporting News on Google div))]:my-4" data-testid="advert--mobile_branded_logo" id="Branded_Logo_Mobile"> The 2-4 Los Angeles Rams are one of the most disappointing teams in the NFL this season. Meant to be a top Super Bowl contender, there's a real chance that the Rams aren't even a playoff team when it's all said and done. But their season isn't over yet. However, the team did just get a crushing piece of news following Week 6, as star wide receiver Davante Adams was revealed to have suffered a serious, multi-week hamstring injury. Rams expected to make trade calls for WR help after Davante Adams injury "I do not expect the Rams to go down without a fight, and my understanding is that they will at least explore the possibility of trading for a wide receiver in the wake of Davante Adams' hamstring injury," Graziano reports. This is a noteworthy development for the Rams, as it shows the team is still trying to compete and make the playoffs from their 2-4 record, despite the 6-0 San Francisco 49ers dominating and the NFC Wild Card being a very tight race. But the Rams potentially adding wide receiver help shouldn't come as a huge surprise, as they had already been one of the teams linked to WRs on the trade market, even before the Adams injury. This is an all-in team after their blockbuster trades for Myles Garrett and Trent McDuffie. Spending a few more draft picks on WR help wouldn't be a surprise whatsoever. They've already mortgaged their future on this 2026 roster. MORE : ESPN analyst believes Browns are a quarterback away from being Super Bowl contenders While the Rams might not land a blockbuster name like Brian Thomas Jr., someone like Jerry Jeudy would be a solid veteran presence in the WR room to help in the meantime while Adams sits on IR with a serious hamstring injury. They're already all-in for 2026; there's no reason why they shouldn't invest a bit more to bolster a roster that can still do some damage if they make the playoffs. Graziano is reporting that WR help is something Les Snead and Sean McVay will consider adding. While the 2-4 Rams might not seem like a buyer, this team is in too deep to not continue striving for a title in 2026. away.headline: Report: Rams WR Puka Nacua's injury not believed to be serious
away.blurb: Nacua sustained the injury during Thursday's practice and did not participate in Friday's session as the Rams (2-4) prepared to face the Raiders (3-3). The Rams already are without fellow wideout Davante Adams, who was placed on injured reserve earlier in the week with a ruptured hamstring. Remaining Los Angeles wide receivers include Konata Mumpfield, Jordan Whittington, Tutu Atwell, CJ Daniels and Alex Bachman. Nacua, 25, has 37 catches for 417 yards and one touchdown to go with one rushing score in four games this season. He missed two games with a hip/groin injury. A two-time Pro Bowl selection, Nacua led the NFL with 129 receptions last season and racked up 1,715 receiving yards with 10 touchdowns in 16 games. home.headline: NFL suspends Buffalo Bills safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson for 1 game for spitting at Las Vegas Raiders
home.blurb: After splitting the 2024 season between the Rams and Baltimore, White re-signed with the Bills and had 16 starts last season. He didn’t rule out another return to Buffalo after completing his one-year contract last season. Today's E-Editions Chicago Tribune Advertise with Us Advertise with Us Branded Content Paid Partner Content Print (Opens in new window) Print Email a link to a friend (Opens in new window) Email ORCHARD PARK, N.Y. — The NFL on Monday suspended Buffalo Bills safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson for one game without pay for spitting in the direction of Las Vegas Raiders players on the field during a game a day earlier. Gardner-Johnson was ejected late in the second quarter for unsportsmanlike conduct following an exchange with a group of Raiders players, including tight end Brock Bowers. In issuing the suspension, the league cited its rule applying to “any act which is contrary to the generally understood principles of sportsmanship.” With Buffalo (5-1) entering its bye week, Gardner-Johnson’s suspension will begin on Oct. 26 and run through Nov. 2, a day after the Bills host the Baltimore Ravens. The player has the right to appeal the suspension. Gardner-Johnson apologized to his teammates immediately following Buffalo’s 33-30 win, and has since posted a note on social media apologizing to fans. “I owe my teammates an apology and to be a man about it,” Gardner-Johnson said following the game. “You got to understand that as a grown man you can’t be doing (stuff) like that in a game,” he added. “As a vet, I’ll be better. I’ll take my consequences as it is, handle it like a man and move on.” The 28-year-old won a Super Bowl with the 2024 Philadelphia Eagles and is on his sixth team in eight seasons. Gardner-Johnson was signed by the Chicago Bears in October 2025 and appeared in 10 games with 51 total tackles. He signed a one-year contract with Buffalo in March. Coach Joe Brady referred to Gardner-Johnson’s spitting act as being “inexcusable,” and said he’s discussed the matter privately with the player. “It can’t happen. That’s not what we’re about. That’s not what the game of football is about, and he knows that,” Brady said. Gardner-Johnson arrived in Buffalo with an established reputation of being a noted trash-talker and as someone who has on occasion crossed the line with illegal hits. “I don’t need a roster of everybody being the same person,” Brady said. “Obviously, he crossed the line yesterday and that can’t happen. It won’t happen again. Personality-wise, I’m not afraid to have people who are going to try to toe the line in everything they do.” Also, the Bills are bringing back a familiar face with cornerback Tre’Davious White agreeing to sign to the team’s practice squad, a person with knowledge of discussions told The Associated Press. home.headline: Rams get bad news on key defensive piece days before Raiders game
home.blurb: According to ESPN’s Adam Schefter , the Rams have placed defensive end Kobie Turner on injured reserve. With this news, Turner will officially be out for a minimum of four games for LA. The Los Angeles Rams will face the Las Vegas Raiders for their Week 7 matchup on Sunday. The Rams desperately need to pick up a win against the Raiders, as they are entering the contest with losses in three of their last four games. With this, they currently have a 2-4 record, which is far below expectations. Now, as the Rams prepare for their game against the Raiders, they have gotten some bad injury news regarding one of their key defensive players. With Turner being a solid part of the Rams’ defense, it is certainly concerning that he is going to miss at least four games due to injury. This is especially so with the Rams desperately aiming to get their season back on track. Turner is currently in his fourth season with the Rams after being drafted by them in the third round of the 2023 NFL Draft, 89th overall. In six games this season, the 6-foot-2 defensive end has posted 22 combined tackles. This is after he posted seven sacks and 48 combined tackles in 17 games for the Rams during last season. They will compete in a Sunday Night Football matchup for the second time in 2026 as they head to Seattle to take on the reigning Super Bowl champions. While Andy Reid's squad has yet to drop a game, the Seahawks have struggled to get their offense going in the post-Kenneth Walker era . Amid their two-game losing streak, quarterback Sam Darnold has tossed four interceptions, including one that ultimately gave the Broncos a free victory last week in overtime. Sportsbooks have labeled Seattle as a slight home favorite, but what does the ESPN Matchup Predictor think? Here's what their computer model projects a few days before kickoff. Chiefs at Seahawks SNF: ESPN Matchup Predictor Gives Prediction This is technically the second meeting between these two teams this year, following an ugly preseason tie in August that featured mostly second and third-string players. Aug 28, 2026; Kansas City, Missouri, USA; Kansas City Chiefs head coach Andy Reid watches play against the Seattle Seahawks during the game at Arrowhead Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Denny Medley-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect ESPN Matchup Predictor Chances at Victory: Chiefs 52.8%, Seahawks 46.8%. ESPN Matchup Predictor Chances at Victory: Chiefs 52.8%, Seahawks 46.8%. While Seattle boasts one of the best home-field advantages in the sport, the matchup predictor still gives the undefeated Chiefs a slight edge to maintain their perfect record. Chiefs on SI's Take Usually, the matchup predictor closely mirrors what traditional betting lines are forecasting. However, that isn't the case for this contest. This was undoubtedly circled as one of the more difficult challenges on the Chiefs' schedule heading into the season, and that stands true despite Seattle's early shortcomings. They have the same defensive playmakers who made them a force to be reckoned with in last year's postseason. Even with Darnold's inconsistencies through the air, Jaxon Smith-Njigba remains a premier wide receiver in the league. He leads the NFL in receptions, receiving yards, and receiving touchdowns in spite of the shaky quarterback play. Seattle's passionate 12s will undoubtedly come out in full force, as this game means a lot more to them than it does to the Chiefs. Kansas City obviously wants to preserve its flawless record, but a loss that drops Seattle to 3-4 would likely take the Seahawks out of the division race moving forward. Walker's homecoming to the team he spent his first four years with is a major storyline. He'll be looking to prove why Seattle should have paid him as he continues to establish himself as one of the best running backs in the NFL. The Chiefs have had plenty of breaks go their way and won't stay undefeated forever, but the Seahawks will have a tough time overcoming turnovers from Darnold if they want to win. Unlike some of their past opponents, Patrick Mahomes will make them pay. Both of these teams have playoff expectations in 2026, but they’re in very different spots through six weeks of the season. Seattle is coming off a bad loss to Denver on Thursday Night Football in Week 6, as Sam Darnold threw multiple picks and the Seattle offense struggled to get anything going against an elite Denver defense. That dropped the Seahawks to 3-3, and they’re multiple games out of first place in the NFC West. Meanwhile, the Kansas City defense put on a clinic in Week 6, holding the Los Angeles Chargers to just six points to move to 5-0 in the 2026 season. There is a huge revenge game possibly on Sunday, as Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III returns to Seattle for the first time since he won Super Bowl MVP for the ‘Hawks. The Seahawks let the star back go in free agency, and he’s been a monster for the Chiefs this season, rushing for 665 yards and six scores in just five games. Even though the Chiefs have a better record, Seattle is favored at home in this marquee matchup. Let’s take a look at the opening odds and some things to watch for in primetime in Week 7. Chiefs vs. Seahawks Odds, Spread and Total Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook Chiefs +2.5 (-115) Seahawks -2.5 (-105) Seahawks: -135 42.5 (Over -105/Under -115) The Seahawks opened as just 1.5-point favorites in Week 7 , but the line has already moved to Seattle -2.5. There is clearly some confidence in this Seattle defense with an extended rest at home against Kansas City. The Chiefs have not lost this season, but they are banged up at the receiver position with Rashee Rice missing Week 6 and Tyquan Thornton on injured reserve. Oddsmakers seem to think this is a spot where the Chiefs will lose their first game in 2026. Chiefs vs. Seahawks Betting Preview These are two of the best defenses in the league, which isn’t what you’d usually think about when referring to a Patrick Mahomes-led squad. The Chiefs traded away Trent McDuffie in the offseason, yet they’re third in the league in EPA/Play and success rate and fourth in EPA/Pass. That could be an issue for a Seattle team that is heavily reliant on Jaxon Smith-Njigba, especially since Sam Darnold has thrown seven interceptions already this season. Seattle (No. 2 in EPA/Play on defense) completely shut down Bo Nix and the Broncos in Week 6, but it wasn’t enough with this offense still struggling. Seattle is just 25th in EPA/Play and 20th in success rate on that side of the ball through six games. It makes sense that the defending champs are favored at home, but there is one stat that I can’t look past when it comes to Mahomes. He’s been a road underdog 12 times in his career, going 10-1-1 against the spread and 9-3 straight up. The Chiefs look like one of the best teams in the NFL, and I expect that to remain the case in Week 7. I don’t mind getting 2.5 points with them as an early lean for this primetime matchup. home.headline: Elijah Arroyo injury update: Seattle Seahawks receive devastating news as young tight end faces another major setback in promising NFL career
home.source: A to Z Sports on MSN
home.blurb: Look, this injury hurts because Elijah Arroyo was just starting to carve out a role. The Seahawks took him in the second round of the 2025 NFL draft with the 50th overall pick. That’s real draft capital for a tight end. He tore his ACL in September of 2022 at Miami. That injury limited him to only nine games across the 2022 and 2023 seasons. He bounced back and put together a great college career with the Hurricanes, which is a big reason Seattle used a second-round pick on him. Seahawks tight end Elijah Arroyo will miss the rest of the 2026 season, dealing another significant blow to his development after previous injury setbacks. How much more can Elijah Arroyo’s young career take? The Seattle Seahawks tight end is undergoing shoulder surgery and will miss the rest of the 2026 season, according to ESPN’s Adam Schefter . Arroyo got hurt in last Thursday night’s primetime loss to the Denver Broncos as he was trying to recover a fumble by wide receiver Rashid Shaheed. It’s a brutal way to lose a season, and it’s even tougher for a second-year player who still has a lot to prove. The numbers tell the story. Arroyo will miss 11 games for Seattle, plus any potential postseason run. Seahawks fans won’t see him on the field again until 2027. Arroyo’s development takes a hit As a rookie, he played in 13 games and caught 15 passes for 179 yards and one touchdown. Those aren’t eye-popping numbers, but they’re a reasonable foundation for a first-year tight end learning the NFL game. The 2026 season hasn’t gone the way anyone hoped, though. Through six games, Arroyo had just one catch for 17 yards, obviously much less production than his rookie year. Now he won’t get the chance to turn that around. This shoulder injury is going to set him back a good bit. A second-year jump matters for young tight ends, and Arroyo loses most of that year. Losing those reps hurts. Injury history follows Arroyo from Miami to Seattle Now, Arroyo’s injury history isn’t new . It just hasn’t involved his shoulder until now. Most of his problems have been with his knee. The knee issues followed him to the NFL, though. In December 2025, Arroyo suffered a Grade One knee strain. It resulted in the Seahawks placing him on injured reserve, and him missing the rest of the season. This shoulder injury is a different animal for Elijah Arroyo. It’s the longest absence of his pro career by a wide margin. For a player who has already lost chunks of time in college and the NFL, it’s another frustrating hurdle. What it means for the Seahawks’ tight end room I’m not going to pretend this changes everything for Seattle. It’s obvious Arroyo came in to be the No. 2 tight end, even as a fairly high draft pick. The Seahawks are set at the position with AJ Barner leading the way. Seattle’s passing game will keep running through its top options, and the tight end room isn’t suddenly in crisis mode. The Houston Texans are officially back, as is Caleb Williams with the Chicago Bears , and we have some serious questions about the Los Angeles Rams , who were upset by the Arizona Cardinals at home last Sunday. The Cardinals now have more wins at SoFi Stadium this year than the Rams and Los Angeles Chargers combined. This week, the Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints will play the first-ever NFL game in Paris, the San Francisco 49ers look to remain perfect against the Atlanta Falcons , and Kenneth Walker III aims to lead the Kansas City Chiefs to victory over his former team, the Seattle Seahawks . This could be a revenge game for the ages. Which teams should you pick in Week 7, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Oct. 21 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. New England Patriots at Chicago Bears (-3) (TNF) Dajani (Bears -3): I can't remember the last time I've been this excited for a Thursday night game. Caleb Williams will suit up for the first time at home since his hamstring injury, and this is the first Bears home game since the passing of Mike Ditka. I have concerns about this Bears pass defense and how it will fare against a red-hot Drake Maye , but the fact is that Chicago has allowed 9.3 points per game at home this season. The Bears' offense has also averaged 35 points per game in their four wins, and I think Williams is out to make a statement. This will be a high-flying affair that comes down to the very end, and a push is very much in play. But give me Chicago at home, with the backing of an emotionally charged atmosphere. Remember, the Bears' lone Super Bowl win came against the New England Patriots under Ditka. … Prediction: Bears 28, Patriots 24 Dubin (Bears -3): I also see this being a high-scoring game, with two offenses that can pile up points quickly. Chicago's offense in two non-rain/non-Brian Flores games with Caleb Williams under center has been electric, particularly on the ground, and Caleb Williams opens things up for the passing game. New England is struggling to run the ball, but Drake Maye has been on fire as of late. I'll lean toward the Bears here because of the Patriots' injury issues along the offensive line, which could hold the run game back further and put even more on Maye's shoulders. … Prediction: Bears 31, Patriots 27 Pittsburgh Steelers (-3.5) vs. New Orleans Saints (Paris) Dajani (Saints +3.5): The Steelers are impossible to figure out. From week-to-week — or even half-to-half, as evidenced by last week's overtime victory against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . If you're going to give me the hook at +3.5 in an international game, I'm probably going to take it. The Saints are a perfect 8-0 ATS in their last eight games away from home, and are 3-0 ATS all-time in international games. I think Gayle Benson's recent comments stirred up the locker room, and the Saints responded with a win in which they dropped 34 points — even if it came against the New York Giants . … Prediction: Steelers 23, Saints 20 Dubin (Steelers -3.5): The Saints finally played a game from ahead last week against the Giants, and they didn't necessarily look comfortable doing it. They have mostly been a second-half offensive team throughout this season, struggling early on before piling up yards and points in comeback mode. I don't trust this offense enough to build a lead against Pittsburgh's defense (ninth in yards, 12th in points, fifth in EPA per play) right now, so I'll lean toward this game playing out in a similar fashion to New Orleans' early-season contests, with the Steelers taking a lead and the Saints trying to stage a comeback, only to fail this time around. … Prediction: Steelers 21, Saints 17 San Francisco 49ers (-3) at Atlanta Falcons Dajani (Falcons +3): I'm thinking about backing the Falcons in this spot. The 49ers had an emotional victory over the Seahawks in Week 5 and are now on a short week after Monday night's win against the Washington Commanders . It looked like we were in for a blowout after the 49ers went up 23-3, but Washington then outscored San Francisco, 14-0, while outgaining the 49ers 201 yards to 7 yards. That was ... interesting to see. The 49ers have found a way to keep winning games despite all of the injuries. Nick Bosa , Mike Evans , Deebo Samuel , Upton Stout and Mykel Williams were among the players who did not practice on Wednesday. This week, I'm going to take the points with Atlanta. … Prediction: 49ers 22, Falcons 20 Dubin (49ers -3): This line feels several points too low, even with Mike Evans potentially out in addition to all of the other wide receiver issues. So long as the Niners have Kyle Shanahan calling plays and Brock Purdy , Christian McCaffrey and George Kittle involved, I think their offense cooks. And Atlanta can't quite reach the same level offensively — even with Bijan Robinson and Drake London on hand. The Niners have been excellent against the run this year, and if this game winds up being one where Penix has to match Purdy throw for throw, I don't see that going well for Atlanta. … Prediction: 49ers 26, Falcons 16 Cincinnati Bengals at Baltimore Ravens (-3) Dajani ( Bengals +3): The Bengals are fresh off their bye while the Baltimore Ravens are fresh off ... a loss to the Cleveland Browns . It was their 15th loss when leading by at least seven points in the fourth quarter since 2020, which ranks the most in the NFL. Lamar Jackson has a chance to return this week, but I'm curious to see how "spry" he looks. The two-time NFL MVP was playing some fantastic ball before the unfortunate ankle injury, and it's worth mentioning he's 7-2 in his career against Joe Burrow . I was high on the Bengals entering this season, and I'm not ready to move off that take. I think this Baltimore secondary is in for a tough test in stopping Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins . The former averages 120.4 receiving yards per game vs. the Ravens, while the latter caught two touchdowns the last time he faced them. Higgins actually hasn't faced Baltimore since Oct. 6, 2024! It's been a while. Give me the upset here. We aren't 100% sure if Jackson is even returning to the lineup, and he'll have to face one of the best interior pass rushes in the NFL. Dexter Lawrence , Jonathan Allen and Kris Jenkins Jr. are the only defensive tackle trio to record multiple sacks this season. … Prediction: Bengals 29, Ravens 27 Dubin (Ravens -3): I'm assuming that Lamar Jackson is back for this game. If he's not, then you can switch my pick to the Bengals. If Jackson is in alongside Derrick Henry and Zay Flowers , I just don't think this Baltimore offense can be stopped. When those three have shared the field this season, the Ravens are averaging 9.9 yards per play. NINE POINT NINE. Unfortunately, the sample size is only 63 plays due to injuries to Jackson and Flowers at different times. If there is any team that can compete with an explosive offense, it's probably the Bengals, but I don't see them quite keeping up here. … Prediction: Ravens 30, Bengals 26 Green Bay Packers at Detroit Lions (-3) Dajani ( Lions -3): Just take the Over in this matchup. The Lions really burned me coming off the bye last year, losing to J.J. McCarthy , but I'm going to back them in this spot. The concern is, of course, the defense, which ranks dead last in the NFL with 404.4 total yards surrendered per game. HOWEVER, I will mention that Kelvin Sheppard 's unit forced five straight three-and-outs from the Cardinals in that 45-21 win in Week 5. Plus, Brian Branch is set to return to the lineup as well. Give me the Lions at home. … Prediction: Lions 35, Packers 30 Dubin (Lions -3): This one has all the makings of a shootout, with two explosive offenses going back and forth. Jared Goff and Co. are coming off the bye, and they have scored 31 or more points in four of their five games to date — and they scored 26 while piling up 452 yards in the other one. Nobody except maybe Kenneth Walker III is doing it at a higher level than Jahmyr Gibbs right now, either. Meanwhile, Green Bay can throw the ball all over the yard, and everyone throws it on the Lions. Maybe Green Bay can actually run with some efficiency in Josh Jacobs ' potential return, but it's not like he was all that efficient last season, either. I lean toward the Lions because they can beat you both ways. … Prediction: Lions 34, Packers 28 Kansas City Chiefs at Seattle Seahawks (-2.5) (SNF) Dajani (Chiefs +2.5): The Seahawks looked completely disinterested in that Week 6 loss to the Denver Broncos . Before the season started, this looked like a potential swing game for the NFC East standings, but a lot has changed in six weeks. Dallas is off to a slow start at 2-4, and the defense (31st in EPA/Play) remains one of the worst in the NFL. Dak Prescott and Co. have lost back-to-back primetime games against Tampa Bay (Week 5) and Green Bay (Week 6), looking pretty rough in both appearances. So, can they turn things around on the road against a divisional opponent? The Eagles enter this game on a four-game losing streak, and star quarterback Jalen Hurts is out for the season with blood clots in his lungs. That is a massive blow to the Eagles in the futures market, as they’re now last in the odds to win the NFC East and +15000 to win the Super Bowl. Tanner McKee is set to make another start in Week 7, and this may turn into a lost season for an Eagles team that could decide to trade some veteran pieces to recoup draft capital and lighten the load on the salary cap in years to come. Oddsmakers have set the Cowboys as favorites in this matchup, and a win would put Dallas in a much better position to win the NFC East – which it is still favored to do. Dallas needs to figure things out on offense, as Prescott has struggled with turnovers (not all his fault) in the last few games while the offensive line allowed him to take a ton of big hits in Week 6.
